findings.claim: The Enabling Act's two-thirds majority was "achieved by arresting Communist deputies, banning Social Democrats from the chamber, and securing Catholic Centre Party support".
findings.truth: The SPD was not banned from the chamber. Its 94 deputies attended and all voted against - the lesson's own body text says "Only the SPD voted against" and gives the 444 to 94 result. The KPD's deputies were the ones arrested or in hiding.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'Enabling Act of 1933'; internal contradiction with the same lesson

findings.claim: "On the night of 30 June 1934, SS and Gestapo units murdered Roehm and around 85 SA leaders" (repeated on a flashcard and in a mark scheme).

findings.truth: Defensible: the contemporary Nazi report counted 267 synagogues destroyed, but modern research counts more than 1,400 synagogues and prayer rooms damaged or destroyed. Left as written; a student meeting the 267 figure elsewhere is not contradicted by it.

summary: Nine lessons checked against the OCR History A spec and its assessment tables. The narrative, dates, election figures and every knowledge-check answer key are sound; the damage is concentrated in the exam framing. All nine practice sets were built on another board's question ladder (4, 8, 10 'two reasons' and 16-mark forms) when this depth study is examined only by a 2-mark describe, a 10-mark explain, a source question and an 18-mark essay, so 63 of the 86 edits relabel and recast those questions. Eight exam tips carried invented examiner claims, two of them fake examiner-report citations. Nine factual fixes: the SPD wrongly said to have been banned from the Enabling Act vote, Bruening's 1931 decree count, the Night of the Long Knives toll and Roehm's death date, the Mother's Cross dated 1933 rather than December 1938, Paulus's surrender date, the July Plot arrest and execution figures swapped, the Nuremberg defendant count, and Stresemann's term as Foreign Minister.
